newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Burundian opposition rejects massacre claims.
newsitem.headline: Burundian opposition rejects massacre claims.

text.p: The Burundian opposition National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) on Friday rejected claims that rebels killed 100 civilians in Kayogoro last week, and accused the army of killing 300 people there.

"After a thorough inquiry, the CNDD denies the allegations by army spokesman Lieutenant Isaie Nibizi stating that 100 civilians were massacred by 'rebels' on Friday April 18 at Kayogoro zone in the Makamba province," it said in a statement.
"But the truth is different. At the same time and place Buyoya's army slaughtered not only the 100 civilians but also more than 200 civilians including children, women and the elderly," it added.

The Tutsi-dominated army that put Major Pierre Buyoya in power last July said last Friday that troops found the bodies of 100 civilians it said had been killed by Hutu rebels in the southern province of Makamba.
The army has been fighting Hutu rebels infiltrating Makamba from northwestern Tanzania.

"The 'rebels' are not so mad as to cut the branch of the tree on which they are sitting," the CNDD statement issued in Brussels said. "Indeed it is fitting to recall that the 'rebels' depend on the civilians who nourish and support them."
More than 150,000 people, mostly civilians, have been killed in the civil war between the army and rebels since troops killed Burundi's Hutu president in 1993.
